html:
The Achi are a Maya people of the mountains of Baja Verapaz, Guatemala, around the towns of Rabinal, Cubulco and Salamá. Their language is close to K'iche', and before the Spanish they formed the lordship of Rabinal, a rival of the K'iche' kingdom.

Their great drama, the Rabinal Achí, is one of the few theatre works from before the conquest to survive: a K'iche' warrior is captured by the lords of Rabinal, tried and put to death, all told in dance and speech. UNESCO recognised it in 2005. Rabinal lies in the region the Spanish called Verapaz, "true peace", after Bartolomé de las Casas and his Dominicans won it by preaching rather than conquest in the late 1530s. During the Guatemalan Civil War the army and its militias killed hundreds of Achi villagers in the Río Negro massacres of 1982. The Q'eqchi' are their northern neighbours.
